siteUrl.title: Website of the Biosphere reserve Schorfheide-Chorin
Website of the Long term ecosystem observation

general.abstract:
The UNESCO-biosphere reserve „Schorfheide-Chorin“ was established in 1990 over an area of approx. 1.300 square kilometres, and is one of the largest protected areas in Germany. Situated in the North-eastern part of Brandenburg, including a major part of the regions Uckermark and Barnim, it represents an impressive cultural landscape with more than 320 lakes, thousands of bogs and mires, extended forests, meadows and arable land.
The so-called Schorfheide and the Chorin end moraine curve are two different landscapes, seen under a culture-historical aspect. The Schorfheide stretches along the west side of the motor way A 11 (Berlin-Poland). The Chorin end moraine curve extends East of the motor way. 75 communities and three small towns (Oderberg, Joachimsthal and Greiffenberg) with a total of 35.000 residents are situated in the protected area.
The main concept behind the biosphere reserve is the consideration of human impact on the land. It is meant to encourage producers to work in a sustainable manner. Thus, 79 % of the area can be used by man. To protect natural resources, priority is given to organic agriculture and forestry and to an extensive-pasture economy. One of the most important supporting partners is the association “Kulturlandschaft Uckermark e.V.” (For promotion of the Cultural landscape Uckermark)

eunisHabitat.label: Arable land with unmixed crops grown by low-intensity agricultural methods (I1.3)
Grasslands and lands dominated by forbs, mosses or lichens (E)
Open non-Mediterranean dry acid and neutral grassland, including inland dune grassland (E1.9)
Permanent eutrophic lakes, ponds and pools (C1.3)
Permanent mesotrophic lakes, ponds and pools (C1.2)
Permanent oligotrophic lakes, ponds and pools (C1.1)
Poor fens and soft-water spring mires (D2.2)
Regularly or recently cultivated agricultural, horticultural and domestic habitats (I)
Valley mires, poor fens and transition mires (D2)

environmentalCharacteristics.geology: North-Eastern German Lowland with morainic and sandic bedrock. The glaciers forming the so-called glacial series.
environmentalCharacteristics.hydrology: The melting off of the glaciers created more than 230 lakes in the area of the biosphere reserve. There are more then 3000 small water bodies, as ponds, puddles or water filled kettle holes.
environmentalCharacteristics.soils: The dominating soils were Cambisols, Gleysols, Luvisols and Podzols.
environmentalCharacteristics.vegetation: Vegetation depends on use and management form: mixed forest, deciduous forest, dry grassland and agricultural accompanging plants.
